candidates.comment: Thanks for the report. This matches the Agent-selected/Ask-mode refusal already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/312400. This report adds VS Code 1.142.0 on Windows/WSL2 and the observation that assistant-visible session instructions identified Ask mode; those details should remain part of the investigation there.

Thanks for the detailed comparison. This matches the custom-agent model-mapping failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340844. This report adds a useful Windows/1.142.0 Azure case: `azure/Azure/gpt-6-luna` is listed as available and succeeds as an explicit model override, but fails when selected through agent frontmatter. Those details should remain part of the investigation there.

Thanks for the detailed request. The public runtime-registration capability is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325827, including independent agent implementations, capability discovery, and native lifecycle integration—not just custom model providers. This report adds useful acceptance criteria for Chat and Agents window parity, localhost and remote operation, subscription independence, permitted VS Code/MCP tools, portable sessions, safe secret scoping, and a documented conformance sample; those requirements belong with that API discussion.

Thanks for the detailed color analysis. The same symptom—Dark 2026 variables appearing like unhighlighted plain text—is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318839. This report adds useful JS/TS detail: `variable.other` uses `#C9D1D9` against the `#BBBEBF` editor foreground, while const/readonly variables remain distinctly blue. Consolidating that evidence with the existing palette discussion.

Thanks for the suggestion. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/292921 already tracks sorting Manage Models by its columns, including pricing. Consolidating there, with this report's additional use case of sorting input and output costs independently when a task has a large input but a short answer.

Thanks for the request. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/306934, which requests enterprise-policy support for the same Disable AI Features setting. This report adds the Windows GPO requirement and the education-environment use case, where disabling agents alone still leaves AI UI visible.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307630 covers per-agent skill isolation, including agent-specific skill discovery folders. Your planner using skills A/B and implementer using C/D is a useful example of the same requirement: unrelated skills should stay out of each subagent's discovery context, rather than merely preloading preferred skills.

Thanks for the report. This matches the plan-to-cloud branch-selection problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/296899. This thread adds confirmation on Windows with Copilot Chat 0.40.1, plus the case where dev is the default branch and explicitly requesting main still does not preserve the intended branch.

Thanks for explaining the difficulty of finding a request after voting has ended. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/103784 already asks for requests to keep accumulating support beyond 60 days rather than losing that momentum or starting over. Consolidating there; this report adds the specific concern that locking prevents later reactions and that a replacement request would lose the original votes.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329209 already tracks cron scheduling, including monthly runs, a scheduling UI, and agent-created schedules. Consolidating there, with the explicit requirement from this report that the agent tool accept cron expressions alongside the UI.

Thanks for the report. We're tracking code review ignoring `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/280829. This adds the SCM Review Uncommitted Changes case: match `applyTo` against the reviewed files and include instruction files without `applyTo`.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/310807 already tracks Agent Skills support for the same Source Control Review Changes action, including uncommitted changes. This report adds useful parity context from GitHub code review's Agent Skills support: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-29-copilot-code-review-agent-skills-and-mcp-now-generally-available/.

Thanks for the report. We're tracking this chat-readiness timeout in remote workspaces at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/283560. This report adds a WSL2 UbuntuExternal occurrence on Windows build 26200 with VS Code 1.109.0 and Copilot Chat 0.37.2; the specific cause here has not yet been established.

Thanks for the report. The missing TODO checklist is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326082, where TODO tools run without displaying the checklist. This report adds the Windows/GPT-5.6 Luna scenario and the useful comparison that the checklist appears with the Local harness.

Thanks for the report and workarounds. This matches the older, open report at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/311802: Start Implementation leaves the conversation under Plan-only restrictions instead of enabling implementation.

Consolidating there should retain your Linux Mint/Auto-model reproduction, the model-switch and edit/resend workarounds, and the macOS confirmation linked through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331958, including the failure after manually selecting Agent.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327430, which tracks the picker closing when a drag crosses its edge while the mouse button is still held. Your report reinforces the need to keep edge colors selectable and retain the picker until release; consolidating the discussion there.

Thanks for the minimal reproduction. This is the same missing tree-item argument during refresh tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/153982. Your reproduction adds a focused case: on macOS 15.6.1 with VS Code 1.107.0, refocusing the window starts a three-second getChildren call, and clicking an inline action before it finishes passes undefined. Keeping https://github.com/bmingles/vscode-treeview-bug linked here preserves those details for the fix.

Thanks for the detailed examples. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/2809 already tracks variable substitution in settings, including the same ${config:...} references to custom settings and support for extension settings. Your nested configuration examples and the contrast with terminal settings provide useful context for that request.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This is the script-boundary highlighting problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/70614; an earlier report of the same inline-if failure was also consolidated there. This report adds a complete multi-script example, confirmation on Linux and vscode.dev, and the workaround of placing a semicolon between the closing brace and </script>.

Thanks for the detailed request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/46471 already tracks the same limitation: extensions cannot reuse VS Code's variable resolution for contributed configuration. Consolidating there, with this report's standalone resolver/getResolved alternatives and the unresolved performance and compatibility concerns from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/148514#issuecomment-1116218814 as additional context; this is not a claim that the API has shipped.

Thanks for the report. The off-center notebook toolbar spinner is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/243027. This report adds that it occurs on Windows with VS Code 1.125.1 and is especially visible at higher magnification, while the individual cell execution spinners rotate normally.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/209653, which also reports that binding notebook.section.runCells to a key does nothing and requests running the active cell's enclosing section. This report adds concrete Windows reproduction steps and identifies the missing fallback when no menu context is supplied.

Thanks for the report. This is the same notebook output toolbar listener warning tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/251838, including the CellOutputElement._attachToolbar → PersistedMenuHideState subscription path. This report adds cross-platform stable-release evidence: approximately 11.3K affected users in 1.116.0 and 10,878 in 1.117.0, with buckets 85812010 and 3f2b8ad6.

Thanks for the detailed examples. Height limits and scrolling for non-text notebook outputs are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/190426. This report adds useful plot/image examples and two possible approaches—limiting each output separately or using a combined scrollable region—which should remain part of that discussion. Switching to text/plain is only a workaround because it loses the rich presentation.

Thanks for the report. This matches the notebook output-menu listener warning already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/251838. This occurrence adds a count of 183 listeners with eight attributed to the output-menu subscription path; as noted above, eight simultaneous output menus can be legitimate, so that stack alone does not establish where a leak originates.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/229176: opening inline chat near the top of a notebook can push cell content outside the visible viewport. This report also notes that scrolling or another re-render restores the content, which is useful detail for investigating the shared issue.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The same first-wheel-scroll jump after notebook Find is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/229318. This report adds a useful clean-install case with a single long code cell, navigating through matches including last-to-first wraparound, and a jump on the next wheel notch; the maintainer confirmation here is useful evidence for that investigation.

Thanks for the report and investigation. The notebook-outline listener warning is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/211105, which includes a large-notebook reproduction and the same per-entry menu subscription stack. This report adds cross-platform telemetry for 1.115.0 and an investigation reporting occurrences across 1.113–1.117; those details belong with the existing issue. The cleanup proposal at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/309157 was closed without merging.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/117656 already tracks the same silent submission failure when the Issue Reporter's authentication session becomes invalid. Consolidating there, with the HTTP 401 / Bad credentials reproduction from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/188169 and the recovery options here: fall back to Preview on GitHub or prompt for re-authentication.

Thanks for the report. The missing Help > Report Issue entry and the issue-template guidance are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317321. This report adds the same behavior on VS Code 1.130.0 / Windows build 22631 with extensions disabled; the question about your `telemetry.feedback.enabled` setting remains relevant to diagnosing it.

Thanks for the report. This matches the Issue Reporter preview URL-length failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/247979. Please retain this report's Help > Report Issue > Preview on GitHub reproduction on VS Code 1.128.0 (Windows 10.0.26200) when investigating that issue.

Thanks for the report. The overbroad billing-meta redirects are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/291730, where a maintainer has acknowledged that distinct bug reports are being caught by the billing classification. This report adds the model-access example and the concern about misleading Upgrade messaging; the later clarification that Opus 4.5 and 4.6 were removed from Pro+ is important when assessing the underlying behavior.

Thanks for the request. The existing `outline.icons: false` setting should cover this; its failure to hide the notebook Outline's M-and-arrow icons is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237495. Your report adds that this still occurs in VS Code 1.107.1 with that setting disabled.

Thanks for the report. This is the same misleading Issue Reporter warning tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/174474. Your screenshot shows it appearing with the title “asd”; the existing discussion explains that the warning concerns similar-issue searches, not issue submission.

Thanks for the report and recording. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/229152, which tracks Report Issue failing to bring an existing reporter window back to the foreground. This report adds the fullscreen scenario and the observation that reloading allows a new reporter window to open.

Thanks for the report. The same notebook toolbar sync-icon wobble is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/243027. This report adds a concrete reproduction: select a kernel without ipykernel installed, run cells, and watch the sync icon beside the stop button.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/275823 already tracks duplicate submissions from Issue Reporter, including the repeated-click case confirmed in its linked discussion. Carrying this detail into that investigation: on macOS, a slow browser launch allowed repeated clicks on `Create on GitHub` to produce multiple issues; disabling the button immediately would prevent that path.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/200898, which tracks image attachments being lost when notebook markdown cells are copied. This report adds the same failure when cutting cells and when copying between notebooks, with Jupyter's web interface preserving the images as expected.

Thanks for the report. The same notebook search-start problem is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/154913. This report adds the selected-variable example, where Find should retain occurrence 7 rather than jump to an earlier match, on VS Code 1.98.0 with Jupyter 2025.2.0.

Thanks for the detailed steps and recording. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/236291, which already tracks newly inserted cells showing another cell type's actions or an incomplete toolbar until focus changes. Consolidating there; this report also provides the recording, alternating code/Markdown insertion cases on Linux Mint, and related run/debug and Restart-button observations that recover after switching application windows.

Thanks for the report and screenshots. Search within notebook comparisons is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/190390. This report adds the Timeline entry point and the observation that Ctrl+F stopped working in VS Code 1.96.2 on Windows while ordinary Python-file comparisons still support it.

Thanks for the report. The same failure to refresh notebook Outline symbols after editing a code cell is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/208665. This report also highlights edits to nested functions, which should be covered when verifying the refresh behavior.

Thanks for the report and clarification. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/154913, which tracks both starting notebook search at the current cell and losing the match position after replacement. Your Windows report on VS Code 1.84.1 also confirms that manually advancing to a later match does not prevent Replace from returning to the first match.

Thanks for the report. The same notebook whole-word shortcut failure is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/200295. This report adds an Ubuntu reproduction on VS Code 1.81.1 and 1.82.0-Insiders, including with extensions disabled, and confirms that binding `toggleFindWholeWord` without a when-clause still does not toggle notebook find.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The same notebook replacement-position problem is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/154913. This report adds a useful single-cell case with repeated `# test` lines, starting beyond the second line, and observations on both macOS and Windows.

Thanks for the report and for confirming the workaround. The same end-of-file VoiceOver reading failure is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/274014. Consolidating there with these additional details: disabling `editor.editContext` restores speech and resolves the reported macOS 27 slowdown; opening and dismissing the Command Palette temporarily restores speech, while switching through Explorer does not.

Thanks for the detailed reproductions. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/271715 already tracks the same IME multi-cursor corruption, including the specific trigger of selecting a non-first occurrence before selecting all matches.

Consolidating there with this report's additional evidence: Windows 10/11, four Chinese/Japanese IMEs, and the direct-commit example where inserting one full-width comma at cursors after 2, 5, and 6 in `123456789` produces `1，，34，，，，789` rather than `12，345，6，789`.

Thanks for the detailed proposal. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/244880 already tracks the same behavior: pressing Enter should leave the cursor on an indented line and insert `end` on the following, outdented line. Consolidating there, with this issue's optional `appendTextNextLine` proposal as a concrete approach that preserves existing `appendText` behavior.

Thanks for the report. The extra `*/` when converting `/* ... */` to `/** ... */` is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/156031. Your report adds a recording and an occurrence on VS Code 1.132.0 with macOS Sonoma 14.0. The proposed fix at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/319405 is still open.

Thanks for the request. Pinning symbol hovers is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/133587. This report adds a useful use case for that work: keeping the hover visible while dragging to select and copy symbol details, even when the pointer leaves the panel.

Thanks for the detailed examples. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/133843, which already tracks invalid CSS when Toggle Line Comment encounters existing comments, including the same escaping approach you suggest. Both examples here are useful acceptance cases: wrapping a multiline comment leaves an extra terminator, while selecting individually commented lines can uncomment only the final brace. Consolidating the discussion there.

Thanks for the detailed examples. This is the same relative-alignment problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/63388, including block comments and indentation that falls between tabstops. Your Plain Text reproduction and wrapped-argument example provide useful additional cases for that issue.

For the fixed-width behavior you want, set `"editor.useTabStops": false`; with four-space indentation, selected-line indent/outdent adds or removes up to four leading spaces without snapping each line to a tabstop.

Thanks for the context. The missing transfer of font size and line height to semantic tokens is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/286157, including the reproduction and discussion of TextMate-to-semantic styling. Consolidating this request there so both typography properties remain part of the tracked work.

Thanks for the report. The scrollbar remaining after an overflowing line is shortened is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/13516. This report adds a useful case: Windows 11, word wrap enabled, and splitting a long HTML class or attribute, with switching away and back clearing the scrollbar. The linked fix proposal, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/284614, was closed without merging, so this is consolidation rather than confirmation of a fix.

Thanks for the report and the complete example. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/174667 is open again and tracks the same PHP indentation problem after `break;`. This report adds a Manjaro Linux reproduction on VS Code 1.98.2 showing how typing successive cases compounds the indentation; that example should be retained when addressing the canonical issue.

Thanks for the report. This is the same comment-sensitive indentation detection problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/170776. Your example adds the case of two-space JSON inside PHP comments overriding four-space PHP code; that case belongs with the same detection work.

Thanks for the request. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/238568, whose discussion also describes multiline parameters leaving only the last parameter visible instead of the function name. Your C example and the preference for keeping the function name visible when the full parameter list is too long are useful context for that work.

Thanks for the concrete example. The same option is already requested in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/49661: preserve whitespace-only lines while trimming spaces after code. Consolidating there would retain this example and the implementation history in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/211093, which closed without merging.

Thanks for the request and follow-up examples. Azure AI Foundry support for non-OpenAI models is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/294841, including Claude's `/anthropic/v1/messages` endpoint and the same deployment-URL error. This thread also adds the Business/Enterprise use case, an explicit Azure-provider configuration, and reports that the error persisted through October 3; those details belong with the same work.

Thanks for the detailed report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/302887, including the workaround of renaming through the open chat's title. This report adds macOS confirmation and useful JSONL evidence: the list rename does not write customTitle, while the title-based rename does.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335320 already requests indented `/btw` child entries in the Sessions list and clearer activity indicators. Consolidating there, including this requirement that the main session remain top-level and its working side chats stay discoverable beneath it. Side-chat activity now appears on the parent row, but individual child entries are still missing.

Thanks for the report and the workaround. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/302887: renaming a conversation from the sessions list can revert when it is opened again. This report also confirms that renaming while the conversation and sessions list are both visible preserves the title; that detail is useful for the shared investigation.

Thanks for the report. Your follow-up at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334193 captures the same search-result line-ending problem on Windows, with additional details about LF changing to CRLF after editing and auto-save on version 1.136.0. Let's consolidate the investigation there.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318355 tracks the same problem: another session's approval controls shift the list, so a click intended for Allow can instead mark a session as done. This report adds a macOS occurrence on VS Code 1.131.0 and reinforces the difficulty of finding and restoring the accidentally archived session.

Thanks for the report. This matches the pinned-session disappearance during response generation tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325448. This report adds confirmation on macOS arm64 with VS Code 1.129.0, including that the sessions return when generation completes.

Thanks for the report. Claude sessions missing a Delete option are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/300582. This report adds Windows details for VS Code 1.123.0 and Claude Code 2.1.167, including entries that persist after cleanup in Claude Code; those details belong with the same deletion work.

Thanks for the detailed request. User-defined folders and groups for Copilot Chat sessions are already requested in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/308516. This report adds useful specifics to that work: a Move to Group context-menu action, collapsible named sections, membership that persists across restarts, and ungrouped sessions remaining at the top.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/166635: undoing Replace All does not restore the search results, leaving Replace All disabled. This report adds a reproduction on VS Code 1.107.0 with Linux/KDE Wayland and an observation that restarting did not help. The attempted fix at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/283061 was closed without merging; these details should remain linked from the canonical issue.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This is the same Search Editor navigation bug tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/198159: results can resolve against the wrong workspace folder when roots share a name. This report adds confirmation on Windows with VS Code 1.102.3, extensions disabled, and Ctrl+Click on results for distinct files. Giving the workspace folders distinct names in the workspace file is a workaround.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The replace-preview content scrolling out of view around collapsed unchanged regions is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/202753. This report adds a pinned cisagov/thorium revision (`f2090d7`), the regex `(//.*\b)ids\b` with replacement `$1IDs` in `*.rs`, and the per-file Replace All advancement case to check when addressing that issue.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/175794, which tracks inconsistent whole-word regex results between closed files and open editors, including results disappearing when switching between files. Your Windows 11 reproduction with the Chinese query `提交`, both search options enabled, initially closed editors, and https://github.com/1684838553/webTips adds useful coverage to that issue.

Thanks for clarifying. Tasks can run repository scripts, but they do not provide checked-in workspace-local shortcuts. That missing capability is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/23757, including the same concern about globally defined shortcuts behaving differently across projects. Your build.sh and non-build script examples fit that request.

Thanks for the detailed troubleshooting log. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/283735, which tracks Windows Ctrl+Alt shortcuts being interpreted as AltGr character input. Your report adds the Hungarian QWERTZ and UK QWERTY cases on VS Code 1.139.1, including a log showing Ctrl+Alt on AltLeft but no modifiers on KeyI, which then inserts Í.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331621 already tracks promoting automation runs into the sessions list through UI and user interaction. Consolidating this there, including drag and drop, a context-menu action, an action in the automation chat, and the question of whether replying to a run should promote it.

Thanks for the report and the standalone reproduction. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335774, which tracks missing Copilot inline suggestions for custom FileSystemProvider documents while equivalent local files work and Copilot Chat remains available. This report adds confirmation on Windows 11 with VS Code 1.139.1, Zowe and ObjectScript examples, and a self-contained `repro-bug:/repro.ts` provider that avoids needing a mainframe connection: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337933#issuecomment-5831681192.

Thanks for the detailed report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327536 already tracks the same missing accessibility semantics on the Markdown editing host. This report adds the explicit requirements for a configurable name defaulting to “Markdown editor” and a stable textbox identity across Editing and Locked modes; those should be included in that work.

Thanks for the request. This is a task-specific case of https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/84072, which tracks showing command arguments in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor. The useful requirement here is to display the task name for `workbench.action.tasks.runTask` bindings and make it searchable, so different task shortcuts can be distinguished without opening JSON.

Thanks for the detailed report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/203786: the rename input opens in the multi-diff editor, but Enter does not apply the rename. Your macOS 26.2 arm64 / VS Code 1.108.2 reproduction through Source Control → View Changes, including occurrence with extensions disabled while other language features work, adds useful confirmation. A fix is proposed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333617, which is still open.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/301692, which tracks continuous newline insertion after confirming an Explorer rename with Enter on Fedora/KDE/Wayland. This report also notes that pressing another key stops the insertion; that detail should remain part of the investigation there.

Thanks for the report. This matches the Linux dead-key shortcut regression tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/282752, including the Swiss QWERTZ case previously consolidated from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/283809. This report adds confirmation on Ubuntu 25.10 with VS Code 1.109.5, the recorded [Equal]/circumflex representation, and that switching to the no-dead-keys layout restores the shortcut.

Thanks for the report. We're tracking the same inline-edit replacement of Unity's `linearVelocity` with `velocity` in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/279209. This report adds an assignment example affecting both property references, with an automatic, non-cached suggestion on VS Code 1.109.2 and extension 0.37.4.

Thanks for the report. We're consolidating this with https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/283167, which already tracks custom instructions for Generate Docs and includes the same problem generating documentation in a requested non-English language. This report adds a concrete case: Editor → Copilot → Generate Docs produces English despite `github.copilot.chat.codeGeneration.instructions` containing `Always response in zh-tw.`, on Windows 10 with VS Code 1.101.0-insider and Copilot 1.323.1582 pre-release.

Thanks for the report. This matches the macOS Option dead-key shortcut issue tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/41024, including the previously confirmed Option+E case. This report adds the Option+E Option+U uppercase chord and the observation that enabling Caps Lock makes it work.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/213911 already tracks replacing textual arrow-key labels with symbols on non-Mac platforms, including Windows. This report makes explicit that the change should cover LeftArrow, UpArrow, RightArrow, and DownArrow.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/140136 already tracks variable substitution in keybinding command arguments, including `${selectedText}`. Your specific use case—passing the current editor selection to Ctrl+P / Quick Open—belongs in that work too.

Thanks for the report and the additional examples. The macOS behavior is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/41024, whose discussion also covers Option+N producing a tilde and Option+E producing an accent despite assigned shortcuts. This report adds the normal US layout on macOS Sonoma and the `alt+f alt+e` focus-editor chord leaving composition active until switching tabs.

The Windows Ctrl+Alt+L observation is not yet established as the same defect.

Thanks for the detailed reproduction. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/193521, which tracks invalid When expressions producing blank, stuck shortcuts that cannot be edited, reset, or removed. This report adds a Windows reproduction using the built-in `actions.find` command with extensions disabled: record Ctrl+F and enter `editorFocus || !!editorIsOpen`. Removing the offending entry from `keybindings.json` is the documented workaround.

Thanks for the detailed captures. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328393, which already tracks missing foreground-model chat spans while gpt-4o-mini utility spans continue to arrive. The additional evidence here is the Windows reproduction across GPT-5 and Claude on Copilot Chat 0.61.0/0.62.0, plus confirmation that hooks and transcripts lack the needed usage data and that xiufengsun/TokenTracker#527 (https://github.com/xiufengsun/TokenTracker/pull/527) only improves discovery and deduplication, not missing telemetry emission.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/302104 tracks both APT update availability and VS Code advertising updates before the package manager offers them, so let's consolidate there. This report adds the Linux Mint 22.3 reproduction and a Debian Trixie observation that repository entries disappear over time; the cause of that deletion remains unconfirmed.

Thanks for the report. This is the same search-editor outline navigation error tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/154348. This thread adds a Windows 24H2 reproduction on VS Code 1.95.3 and a later confirmation that the error prevents navigating large search results by file.

Thanks for the report and the keyboard workaround. Directly revealing a breadcrumb folder in Explorer is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/67711. This report adds the case where Explorer is in the secondary sidebar, plus the keyboard workaround described above; both remain useful context for that work.

Thanks for the feedback. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/309223 already tracks reducing stable update frequency and providing slower release channels. This thread also highlights the cost of reconnecting remote and container sessions after update restarts; that feedback belongs in the same discussion.
